Q: Break a previous commit into multiple commits A:

Git 2.54 introduces the git history split <commit> command.

It presents an interactive interface, similar to the one used in git add -p to selectively add/remove hunks that were part of the original commit.

git history split 10a4041

diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index cea5240..d355ab2 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -3,6 +3,7 @@
 ## Try `git history`

 Attempting to edit a commit message using `git history` command.
+Edit the readme again.

(1/1) Stage this hunk [y,n,q,a,d,?]?

After selecting the hunks, you will be asked for two commit messages: one for the hunks selected, and the other for the hunks left unselected. After editing the commit messages, run git push --force-with-lease to update the commit history. Descendent branches, if any, will be updated to point at the updated history.

Limitations:

  1. As of this writing, git history split does not support histories containing merge commits.

  2. It does not support operations that would result in a merge conflict.

More Info:

  1. https://github.blog/open-source/git/highlights-from-git-2-54/

  2. https://about.gitlab.com/blog/whats-new-in-git-2-54-0/

  3. --force-with-lease: https://stackoverflow.com/a/52937476/6513921

Q: Common scenarios for memory leaks in Vanilla JavaScript and how to properly clean up? A:

Global variable is the killer in most of the cases especially when you have many function is referring and adding data to that variable. Solution (or better practice) for that is to use recursive function with memory parameter, so the usage of the param can be scoped better and automatically cleared when the entire workflow/process is finish.

Q: In Python while unsing the PIL pillow library. When I open an image and call load on it do it still need to close it? A:

I think my example was not very reflective of what i was trying to do. Basically I wanted to eagerly load images threaded like this:

def load_eager(path)
    image = Image.open(path)
    image.load()
    return image

And wondered if i could just lose the reference to the future instead of what i was doing: future.result().close() if the image ends up not beeing needed. This seems to be the case.

A better approach would maybe be:

def load_eager(path, container)
    if path in container:
        return
    with Image.open(path) as image:
        image.load()
    container[path] = image
    return

Or doing with it asyncio.
